governing_relation_note: 225 = I_rms^2 at the 15 A contract ceiling. Writing 450*R_hot is the special case R_HS = R_LS = R_hot. The high-side and low-side devices are separated here because their gate-source biases (and so Rds(on)) differ.

primary_sources_captured.document: NXP TEA2209T Active bridge rectifier controller, Product data sheet, Rev. 1.1, 14 April 2021, 19 pp
Infineon IPW60R017C7 600V CoolMOS C7 Power Transistor, Final Data Sheet, Rev. 2.0, 2016-03-01, 14 pp

envelope.conduction_coefficient_basis: 2 conducting devices, one high side + one low side of a diagonal pair; line-cycle average = (R_HS+R_LS)*I_rms^2 = 225*(R_HS+R_LS); this equals 450*R_hot only when both devices share R_hot.

circuit.topology: Four-MOSFET active (synchronous) full-bridge rectifier replacing the four-diode bridge at the PFC input; the downstream CCM boost PFC is unchanged.

controller.function: Senses mains polarity between pins L and R and drives the diagonal pair; full-wave drive of all four bridge MOSFETs.

circuit.node_map: AC line into L (pin 1) and R (pin 12), the switching nodes / sources of the two upper MOSFETs. Upper MOSFETs connect VR (DC+) to L/R; lower MOSFETs connect L/R to GND; VR is the rectified output feeding the boost. Off device blocks the line voltage (<=186.7 V steady).
circuit.conduction_pair: one high-side and one low-side device of a diagonal pair, in series with the line current; the other two block.

high_side_gate_drive_path.description: NOT a resistor divider and NOT the same as the low side. Each high-side driver is powered by a FLOATING supply (VCCHL/VCCHR) referenced to its own switching node (L or R). That floating supply is a BOOTSTRAP capacitor (100-220 nF typical; 200 nF in NXP's Figure 3/5 typical configuration; 2.2 uF is the separate VCC supply capacitor) charged from VCC through an internal bootstrap diode while the high-side device is OFF and its source node is pulled to the return rail. The high-side gate driver is a rail-to-rail MOS output referenced to the floating supply; the gate is therefore driven to VCCHL relative to L/R.
high_side_gate_drive_path.gate_charge_losses_are_a_design_constrai: TEA2209T Section 12, page 12: 'Bootstrap capacitors with lower value may cause a voltage drop that is too high because of the gate charge losses.'

circuit.low_side_gate_drive_path: Low-side drivers are referenced to GND and powered directly from VCC (Vregd). VCC is recharged from the rectified line at each zero crossing and discharges during the half cycle.

dead_time.condition: zero-crossing comparator delay; 550-1200 ns at dV/dt=10 V/us, 1200-2500 ns at dV/dt=0.1 V/us

circuit.fail_off: Gate pull-down currents to <2 V when a driver supply is below UVLO; D-S overvoltage protection disables all drivers; on loss of supply the body diodes revert the bridge to a passive diode bridge (TEA2209T Sections 8.3.1-8.3.3).

gate_supply_result.the_correction: Vregd (typ 10.7 V) is the regulated VCC rail, NOT the MOSFET gate-source voltage. High-side VGS is set by the floating bootstrap supply, which is (VCC - Vd(bs)) minus the gate-charge droop Qg/C_bs and the floating-supply leakage over the on-time.
gate_supply_result.method: Solve VGS = (VCC - Vd) - Qg(VGS)/Cbs - I_leak*T_on/Cbs self-consistently; T_on = 8.333 ms (half of a 60 Hz line cycle); Qg(V) taken from IPW60R017C7 Table 6 + Diagram 10.

high_side_vgs_v.conditions: for the worstcase row: VCC min 10.2 V, Vd max 1.3 V, Cbs 100 nF, II(VCCHL) max 12 uA

low_side_vgs_v.basis: VCC minus the 2-gate-charge + bias droop of the 2.2 uF CVCC over one half cycle

is_the_10V_data_applicable.low_side: YES, approximately (slightly conservative): low-side VGS ~ 10.4-10.9 V >= 10 V.
is_the_10V_data_applicable.high_side: NO, not directly. High-side VGS is ~8.5 V typical with the datasheet's own 200-220 nF bootstrap value. Rds(on) must be corrected for the lower bias.

correction_factor.basis: IPW60R017C7 Diagram 7 family (Tj=125 C): at ID~21 A, Rds(7V)/Rds(10V) ~ 1.02; the C7 die is near-fully enhanced above ~7-8 V, so the penalty is small. Digitised, evidence class manufacturer_datasheet_figure_digitized.

is_the_10V_data_applicable.design_consequence: If the bootstrap capacitor is sized at the datasheet minimum (100 nF), the high-side VGS falls to ~7.3 V typ (6.3 V worst case) and the penalty grows; a value at or near the 220 nF upper bound should be specified.

sourced_bounds.note_186_7_not_170: The previous attempt used 170 V (120 Vrms peak). The contract's high line is 132 Vrms -> 186.7 V.
sourced_bounds.retained_bridge_source: GBU2510A declared '1000 V / 25 A' in zapote/power-entry/BOM.md; the GBJ2510-F datasheet (semiconductor-research.md) gives VRRM 1000 V, IFSM 350 A, I2t 510 A2s.

controller_node_limit_v.source: TEA2209T Table 6 (absolute maximum) and Section 12 ('Mains transients or surges must be limited to voltages below 700 V')

voltage_contract.declared_contract_statement: Design to line 108/120/132 Vrms 50/60 Hz. The off bridge device blocks the line peak in normal operation. The retained board implies, but does not document, a transient contract: it carries a 1000 V-class passive bridge and declares NO surge clamp/varistor. The controller itself requires mains-node transients below 700 V. Fault conditions: loss of drive reverts to a body-diode bridge (safe); a boost-switch short or bus fault can connect the ~400 V bus (bounded by the 450 V bulk capacitors) to the bridge output.

nxp_700V_node_limit_binding.basis: the device must block the node voltage the controller permits

added_clamp_limiting_node_to_500V.basis: requires a clamp that is NOT in the retained BOM

retained_bridge_equivalent_no_clamp.basis: match the retained passive bridge's implied 1000 V design point

voltage_contract.conclusion: The required device rating is NOT settled by the line range. The retained design point implies 1000 V (no clamp); NXP's own stated node limit implies >=800 V; the 600 V reference candidate is valid ONLY under an added clamp that limits the bridge node to <=500 V, which is not declared in the retained BOM.

body_diode.conditions: VR=400 V, IF=58.2 A, diF/dt=100 A/us
body_diode.selection_risk: slow body diode (no fast-recovery body diode); retained as a risk for an active bridge

candidates.contract_status: Satisfies the voltage contract ONLY under an added <=500 V clamp. Insufficient against the retained 1000 V design point and against NXP's 700 V node limit.

candidates.screen_result: NOT SUPPORTED by the explicit contract. A 500 V-class device satisfies only the line-only variant; it fails the retained-bridge-equivalent (1000 V) and NXP-node-limit (800 V) variants, and in the <=500 V-clamp variant it adds no margin over the 600 V reference (500 V rating against a 500 V clamp). Per the task it is not screened further and no rating is assumed.

gate_network_and_controller.note: TEA2209T 2 mW IC + four gate charges per line cycle at 60 Hz. Line-frequency gate drive is milliwatt-scale, not watt-scale.

dead_time_body_diode.condition: about the zero crossing where i(t)=Ipk*sin(wt)~0; td<=2.5 us; VSD typ 0.9 V

line_commutation_reverse_recovery.condition: IPW60R017C7 Qrr typ 18 uC is specified at IF=58.2 A, VR=400 V, diF/dt=100 A/us; the real commutation is at the line zero crossing (low current, low voltage), so this is an over-bound, not the operating value

startup_inrush_body_diode.condition: NTC-limited (SL32 10015, 10 ohm) inrush through the body diodes before VCC charges
startup_inrush_body_diode.missing_evidence: no inrush waveform/energy captured; no bench work permitted

emi_filter_obligation.conditions: line-frequency MOSFET commutation changes the conducted/radiated EMI picture; any added filter/snubber loss is not sourceable

eoss.note: commutation is at low node voltage, so Eoss at 400 V (30 uJ) is not the operating event; not separately quantified

assembly.concept: Reuse the selected bridge cooling concept (thermal/bridge-cooling.md, 2026-09-14): Wakefield 395-1AB heatsink, 2x Sunon MF80251V1 fans, aluminium spreader, Bergquist SIL PAD TSP 1800.
assembly.Ta_basis: design inlet air maximum, selected cooling contract
assembly.Rsa_basis: catalog 0.50 K/W at 500 LFM; a TYPICAL catalog condition, not a guarantee in the duct
assembly.Rcs_basis: ASSUMED TO-247 case-to-spreader/sink contact budget for four devices; sensitivity 0.25..1.0 K/W. The selected cooling contract's 0.25 K/W case-to-sink is for the larger GBU case and is not directly transferable.

computed_result_98pct_sensitivity.note: Diagram 8 98% curve, a distributional percentile NOT a guaranteed maximum

thermal_path_assumptions.method: T_sink = Ta + P_total*Rsa; Tj_i = T_sink + P_i*(Rjc+Rcs); Rds(Tj) re-evaluated from the digitised Diagram 8 and iterated to convergence. Per-device line-cycle average P_i = 0.5*R_i*I_rms^2.
thermal_path_assumptions.limitations: DC Rth used against line-cycle-average power; the 8.33 ms pulse is smoothed by Zth(j-c) but that is not modelled. The four TO-247 devices are assumed to sit on the same spreader/sink with total Rsa=0.50 K/W; sharing with the boost switch is not modelled and would raise the sink temperature.

savings_step6.residual_uncertainty: P_additional beyond the quantified ~2.5 mW (start-up inrush, EMI/filter, and the operating reverse-recovery value rather than its 43 mW over-bound) is unknown and subtracts from every row. The device-parameter basis is typical (the 98% row shows the 25% spread); no guaranteed hot maximum exists for any candidate. The voltage-rating condition (added clamp) is a gating, not a loss, uncertainty.

unknowns: Operating value of the line-commutation body-diode reverse recovery (only the 58.2 A / 400 V rated Qrr is published; the real event is at the zero crossing).
Start-up/inrush body-diode loss (no captured inrush energy; no bench work permitted).
EMI re-qualification and any added filter/snubber loss from replacing diode commutation with MOSFET commutation.
Guaranteed hot maximum Rds(on) for the reference candidate (only typical hot data and a 98% curve exist).
The actual installed Rcs of four TO-247 devices on the spreader (assumed 0.5 K/W).
The product's real surge/transient test level and the presence/absence of a front-end clamp (not declared in the retained BOM).
